description: TLS connections the extension inspects before writing anything on them. Only towards hosts for which the extension holds the https:// host permission (checked again on every write and read; once it is gone the connection is closed). Accepted from the background page only, as defence in depth: any page of the extension can reach the background page, so the extension as a whole is the trust boundary. Arguments are checked by the implementation (not by this schema) so that every refusal is an ExtensionError whose message starts with a code: CONFIG, PERMISSION, PROXY_AUTH, PROXY, TLS, NETWORK, TIMEOUT or CLOSED.

functions.name: open
functions.description: open({host, port, timeoutMs}) connects to host:port, directly or through the proxy Thunderbird would use for https://host:port/ (SOCKS, or an HTTP proxy tunnel), completes the TLS handshake and resolves to {id, route, securityInfo}. route is "direct", "socks" or "http-proxy"; securityInfo has the shape of webRequest.getSecurityInfo(requestId, {certificateChain: true}), with the chain Gecko verified. Not one application byte has been written. Only a connection Gecko judges secure with a verified chain is returned: a refused chain, a certificate exception, a broken or weak connection are TLS rejections. Connections are anonymous: no client certificate. host: lower-case ASCII host name, IPv4 address or bracketed IPv6 address, exactly as in the origin; port: 1-65535, not one Gecko bans for https; timeoutMs: 1000-120000 (default 30000), deadline for the whole opening.

functions.name: write
functions.description: write(id, bytes) writes all the bytes (a Uint8Array or an ArrayBuffer of at most 1 MiB) on an open connection. One write at a time per connection: a second write() while one is pending is a CONFIG error; larger bodies are written in sequence. Resolves once every byte has been handed to the connection: at most 256 KiB are then still waiting to go out.

functions.name: read
functions.description: read(id, {maxBytes, timeoutMs}) resolves to the next bytes received, a Uint8Array of 1 to maxBytes (1-1048576, default 1048576) bytes, or to null once the peer has closed the connection. null is NOT an authenticated end of message (the peer may close without TLS close_notify): the caller must frame what it reads. One read at a time. timeoutMs: 1-600000, default 60000.

functions.name: close
functions.description: close(id) closes the connection. Closing an unknown or already closed connection does nothing.
